item.title: Tavua Town Council says it would never risk lives amid Garvey Park safety concerns
item.description: The Tavua Town Council says they would never imperil the health of anyone's life or limb if they had knowledge of the dangers posed from the use of any of its assets, in this case Garvey Park. item.content:encoded:
The Tavua Town Council says they would never imperil the health of anyone's life or limb if they had knowledge of the dangers posed from the use of any of its assets, in this case Garvey Park.

This is after concerns were raised in regards to the safety of students playing over the weekend at Garvey Park in Tavua which was the venue of some of the Vodafone Super Deans quarterfinals as well as the Weetbix Raluve competition, where students were seen digging out large stones from the ground.

While responding to fijivillage News, Acting Council CEO, Sireli Korovulavula says they are also deeply concerned about the discovery of the stone in the centre of the playing field before the start of the games on Saturday.

Korovulavula says the ground has within the last few weeks hosted Kaji Rugby for the Tavua/Vatukoula District an d the Western Secondary School League games and there was no indication of the presence of the stone during the two sporting events.

He says in hindsight, they are in total agreement that more vigilance ought to have been taken by the Council and that is what it will do going forward.

Assistant Minister for Youth and Sports, Aliki Bia had raised the alarm early Saturday morning after students were seen digging out large stones f rom the ground saying this is not good and it does not portray a good image for the development of our rugby.

Bia says the welfare of students and players is paramount.

item.title: Emerging rugby talent to take centre stage alongside Fijiana XV
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 11/08/2026 The Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Interim Committee has clarified that, as part of the Vodafone Super Deans semi-final programme, selected matches will be played alongside the second Test between the Vodafone Fijiana XV and South Africa’s Springbok Women this Saturday at Churchill Park in Lautoka.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 11/08/2026

The Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Interim Committee has clarified that, as part of the Vodafone Super Deans semi-final programme, selected matches will be played alongside the second Test between the Vodafone Fijiana XV and South Africa’s Springbok Women this Saturday at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

This gives Fiji’s emerging rugby talent a unique opportunity to perform on one of the country’s biggest rugby stages.

Interim Committee representative Biu Colati says the programme has been designed with the long-term development of school rugby at its heart.

He says their priority has always been to provide the best possible experience for student-athletes while continuing to strengthen the development pathway for school rugby.

Colati says the programme gives young players the rare opportun ity to perform on the same stage as the national team, exposing them to the atmosphere and standards of international rugby while celebrating the very best of school rugby.

He adds that the experience will inspire many of these players as they continue their rugby journey.

Colati says they sincerely thank the Ministry of Education, the Fiji Rugby Football Union, participating schools, competition officials, sponsors, volunteers and supporters for working together to make the programme possible.

Looking at the semi-finals at Churchill Park in Lautoka, Ratu Navula College will face Ratu Kadavulevu School in the Under-14 grade, Ratu Navula College will meet Lelean Memorial School in the Under-19 division, Sigatoka Methodist College will play St Vincent College in the Weet-Bix Raluve Under-16 and Suva Grammar School will take on Ra High School in the Under-18 grade.

At 1pm on Saturday, the Vodafone Fijiana XV will take on the Springbok Women in the second Test of the series.

The remaining Vodafone Super Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve semi-final fixtures will be played at HFC Bank Stadium, Buckhurst Ground 1 and Bidesi Ground in Suva.

In the Super Deans semi-finals in Suva, Queen Victoria School will face MGM High School in the Under-14 grade.

In the Under-15 grade, Lelean Memorial School will meet Marist Brothers High School, while QVS will face Ratu Kadavulevu School.

In the Under-16 grade, Nasinu Secondary School will take on Suva Grammar School, while QVS will meet MGM High School.

In the Under-17 grade, Ba Methodist High School will play RKS, while QVS will face Suva Grammar School.

RKS will meet Navatu Secondary School in the Under-19 grade, while Lelean Memorial School will face Nasinu Secondary School in the Under-18 grade.

In the Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals, Adi Cakobau School will face Nasinu Secondary School in the Under-16 grade.

In the Under-18 grade, MGM High School will meet ACS, while Sila Central High School will take on Lomary Secondary School.

item.title: Tavatavanawai and Narawa set for All Blacks return against Sharks
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 11/08/2026 Timoci Tavatavanawai and Emoni Narawa have been named in the 23-member All Blacks squad that will face the Sharks tomorrow in their second match of the Greatest Rivalry Tour.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 11/08/2026

Timoci Tavatavanawai and Emoni Narawa have been named in the 23-member All Blacks squad that will face the Sharks tomorrow in their second match of the Greatest Rivalry Tour.

Tavatavanawai has played twice for the All Blacks, while Narawa has four caps.

Both players have been named on the bench and are expected to light up the stadium when they take the field.

Meanwhile, Head Coach Dave Rennie has made 14 changes to the starting 15 that defeated the Stormers last weekend, with Ruben Love starting at flyhalf and partnering with Kyle Preston at halfback.

Ethan de Groot will team up with Asafo Aumua and Fletcher Newell in the front row, while Josh Lord and Sam Darry will start at lock.

Tupou Vaa’i and Luke Jacobson will start at flanker, while Wallace Sititi retains his number eight jersey.

Caleb Clarke and Fehi Fineanganofo will start on the wings, with Jordie Barrett partnering Quinn Tupaea in the centres, while Damian McKenzie starts at fullback.

The All Blacks will face the Sharks at 5am tomorrow before taking on the Bulls at 5am this Sunday , followed by the Lions on August 26th at 5am.

Their first Test against South Africa will be on August 23rd at 3am.

They will then play the second Test on August 30th at 3am, followed by the third Test on September 6th at 3am, with the fourth and final Test scheduled for September 13th at 3am.

item.title: Rewa FC apologises to supporters after 4-1 loss
item.description: Rewa FC has apologised to its supporters following its 4-1 defeat to Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC in its opening OFC Men’s Champions League 2026 match. The Delta Tigers have expressed their gratitude to the supporters who travelled to Churchill Park in Lautoka, wore the team colours and continued to back the side throughout the match.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC has apologised to its supporters following its 4-1 defeat to Vanuatu’s Galaxy FC in its opening OFC Men’s Champions League 2026 match.

The Delta Tigers have expressed their gratitude to the supporters who travelled to Churchill Park in Lautoka, wore the team colours and continued to back the side throughout the match.

The club says the result and performance were not what the team or its supporters had expected.

They says it is equally disappointed with the result but believes the defeat will not define its campaign.

Rewa says the players will learn from the loss and return stronger for their remaining Group B matches.

The club has also urges supporters to continue believing in the team, saying its heads will not drop and the fight will continue.

Rewa will face Tupapa Maraerenga FC of the Cook Islands tomorrow at 4pm at 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

Tupapa Maraerenga also lost its opening Group B match.

Rewa will play its final group match against Lae City FC of Papua New Guinea on Saturday at 3pm at the same venue.

The Delta Tigers need positive results in both matches to keep their hopes of reaching the semi-finals alive.

item.title: Super Deans and Raluve semi-finals set for Lautoka and Suva this weekend
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 11/08/2026 The Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans semi-finals will be held in Lautoka and Suva this weekend, with the Deans organisers giving women's rugby and emerging rugby talent the opportunity to perform on some of the country’s biggest rugby stages.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 11/08/2026

The Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans semi-finals will be held in Lautoka and Suva this weekend, with the Deans organisers giving women's rugby and emerging rugby talent the opportunity to perform on some of the country’s biggest rugby stages.

Four semi-finals will be held at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

These include the Under-14 semi-final between Ratu Navula College and Ratu Kadavulevu School, followed by the Under-19 clash between Ratu Navula College and Lelean Memorial School.

The Weet-Bix Raluve Under-16 semi-final between Sigatoka Methodist College and St Vincent College will then be played.

At 1pm on Saturday, the Vodafone Fijiana XV will take on the Springbok Women in the second Test of the series.

The day’s final match will feature the Under-18 semi-final between Suva Grammar School and Ra High School.

The remaining Vodafone Super Deans and Weet-Bix Raluve semi-final fixtures will be played at HFC Bank Stadium, Buckhurst Ground 1 and Bidesi Ground.

In the Super Deans semi-finals in Suva, Queen Victoria School will face MGM High School in the Under-14 grade.

In the Under-15 grade, Lelean Memorial School will meet Marist Brothers High School, while QVS will face Ratu Kadavulevu School.

In the Under-16 grade, Nasinu Secondary School will take on Suva Grammar, while QVS will meet MGM High School.

In the Under-17 grade, Ba Methodist High School will play RKS, while QVS will face Suva Grammar.

RKS will meet Navatu Secondary School in the Under-19 grade, while Lelean Memorial School will face Nasinu Secondary School in the Under-18 grade.

In the Weet-Bix Raluve semi-finals, Adi Cakobau School will face Nasinu Secondary School in the Under-16 grade.

In the Under-18 grade, MGM High School will meet ACS, while Sila Central High School will take on Lomary Secondary School.

item.title: Under 18 teams keep cards close to their chest ahead of Deans semi-finals
item.description: fijivillage Sports contacted the participating schools, but most school managements declined to comment, choosing instead to maintain a media blackout as the countdown to the semi-finals begins. The silence has only added to the excitement among former students and supporters, with old scholars working behind the scenes to organise buses and transport for fans travelling to the matches.
item.content:encoded:
fijivillage Sports contacted the participating schools, but most school managements declined to comment, choosing instead to maintain a media blackout as the countdown to the semi-finals begins.

The silence has only added to the excitement among former students and supporters, with old scholars working behind the scenes to organise buses and transport for fans travelling to the matches.

Two Southern Zone finalists, Suva Grammar School and Nasinu Secondary School, will represent the South, while Lelean Memorial School will represent the Eastern Division and Ra High School will carry the hopes of the West.

Suva Grammar School will face Ra High School on Saturday at Churchill Park in Lautoka, while Lelean Memorial School will take on Nasinu Secondary School at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

With the schools keeping their preparations under wraps, anticipation is building as supporters eagerly await what promises to be two highly competitive semi-final clashes.

item.title: Battle for 2nd place and relegation heats up in Extra Premier League
item.description: The battle for second place and the fight to avoid relegation will take centre stage as the 2026 Extra Premier League heads into its final matches. Dayal’s Sawmillers Ba FC has already secured the championship after thrashing Tailevu Naitasiri FC 6-0.
item.content:encoded:
The battle for second place and the fight to avoid relegation will take centre stage as the 2026 Extra Premier League heads into its final matches.

Dayal’s Sawmillers Ba FC has already secured the championship after thrashing Tailevu Naitasiri FC 6-0.

The win took the Men in Black to 39 points and secured their record 22nd national league title with one match remaining against Rewa FC.

Rewa FC and Labasa FC are now locked on 32 points in the race for second place.

Rewa holds the advantage on goal difference and has matches remaining against Navua FC and Ba, while Labasa will face Lautoka and Tailevu Naitasiri for remaining matches.

Lautoka is fourth with 23 points, while Nadi and Nasinu are level on 21 points.

Suva FC moved to 20 points following its 3-2 victory over Nasinu and sits one point ahead of Navua.

With only the bottom-placed team to be relegated to the Senior Division, every point will be crucial in the remaining matches.
